newsitem.title: UK: P&O hit by downbeat statement, fines report.
newsitem.headline: P&O hit by downbeat statement, fines report.

text.p: Shares in Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co. (P&O) fell on Wednesday after the British group said shipping rates were still under pressure and EU sources said the company was likely to be fined.
P&O shares dropped as low as 611p before recovering slightly to trade at 613p, down 6-1/2p or 1.4 percent on the day. The broader market was up 0.3 percent.

P&O said European ferry rates were still under pressure in the third quarter despite a smaller percentage drop in volumes than seen earlier this year. The company said there was also pressure on rates in Far East to Europe container trade.
EU sources said P&O would be one of five ferry operators to pay fines for allegedly operating a price cartel in 1992.
Marketmakers said the third-quarter statement and fine had weighed on P&O stock but noted that the share had gained strongly this year on the container merger with Nedlloyd.

"The statement is less than encouraging but nothing particularly unexpected...The fines news has made headlines but in percentage terms, it shouldn't impact the bottom line too much," one dealer said.
P&O shares have risen 29 percent since the start of the year and touched a record 657p after the Nedlloyd container deal.
"The fines were well flagged and more a gesture, a slap on the wrist. It's nothing major and a way of reminding companies not to overstep the mark," said David Elsmore, analyst at Kleinwort Benson.

Elsmore, who recommends P&O as a strong buy on the back of the Nedlloyd merger, said he did not expect major gains in the short term as investors waited to see how the company would perform rather than "giving them the benefit of the doubt".
But he said the market, focused on the bleak outlook for 1996 and a possibly difficult year in 1997, had so far failed to appreciate the value of the container deal.
Elsmore said the share could succumb to profit-taking, with investors anxious about the company's performance.
